text: Security is a vital part of web development. One basic step is using HTTPS, which encrypts data between the user and the server. Authentication also matters: websites should verify who users are, often with strong passwords or two-factor methods. Input validation is another key practice. It means checking everything users type, so harmful code cannot enter the system. Developers must also learn about common vulnerabilities, such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting. These weaknesses can let attackers steal data or damage a site. By combining HTTPS, careful authentication, strict input validation, and awareness of common threats, developers can build safer web applications for everyone.
